goal: Move the Kiln program from M1 (shadow keys, no merge job) through the PR8 gate to M2/M3 (CI skips ledger hits behind a required check), one reviewable PR at a time.

policy.selection_rule: Highest priority item that is (a) already specified by an accepted spec, (b) fully verifiable locally or in a pull-request CI run, and (c) fails closed if implemented wrong. Soundness-bearing code that cannot be validated before merge (anything `kiln record prepare` only accepts on a trusted default-branch run) is never selected first.
policy.excluded_scope_note: The three excluded classes change what a cache hit MEANS (M3 skipping, deleting the cross-check oracle, and relaxing the unknown-write-set rule). Each needs the PR8 gate's evidence first and is the owner's call, not a loop item.
policy.validation_gate: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -short ./... in code/programs/go/kiln; workflow changes parse and change only CI; security review before every push (CLAUDE.md).

items.title: Census PR E: schedule the weekly Kiln census in the PR8-gate configuration
items.why: The PR8 gate (>=3 clean shards on both runner images, home: runner) is the only thing between the recorder and the scanner deletion, and today it needs a person to dispatch it. Without a schedule the repository produces no automatic evidence for it.
items.scope: .github/workflows/kiln-census.yml schedule trigger + input fallbacks for a non-dispatch event; KILN04 4.8; CHANGELOG.d
items.risk: low: CI configuration and docs only, no build or recorder code
items.outcome: Merged 2026-11-22 as f4d3e1d2ab2. The weekly run is red until the PR8 gate passes, by design.

items.title: Production recmerge.Keys: memoised weak/strong keys per distinct host facts
items.why: recmerge.Merge takes a Keys interface that nothing implements ('memoised per distinct facts (PR 3)'). No shard can become a manifest until it exists.
items.scope: code/programs/go/kiln/internal/legacy (or a new mergecmd package) + tests
items.risk: medium: key bytes are soundness-critical; every path must fail closed on refusal
items.outcome: Landed inside K-03 as internal/record/mergekeys.go (TracedKeys): one *legacy.Traced per distinct facts, so the adapter and the job are reviewable together.

items.title: stage-4 PR 3a: `kiln record-merge` + production recmerge.Keys
items.why: The last executable gap between 'shards record' and 'the ledger has manifests'. Until it lands, stage 5a lookup has nothing to look up and all recorder work stays inert.
items.scope: new CLI subcommand over internal/recfmt + internal/recmerge + internal/ledger; the CI jobs
items.risk: high: a merge bug produces false hits; the CI half cannot be validated on a branch because prepare refuses an untrusted run
items.note: Both landed in one PR because the Keys alone would be dead code. The remaining half of K-03 -- the `kiln-record.yml` / merge CI jobs -- is K-12.

items.title: M0: pin the wasm lane into code/kiln/legacy/pinned.json
items.why: pinned.json was still {"languages": []}, so every package planned as `unpinned` and no pinning precondition could ever hold.
items.scope: 147 cargo lines in code/packages/wasm/*/BUILD and BUILD_windows get --locked; gf256 and polynomial gain the Cargo.lock they never had; pinned.json gains wasm; KILN03 7.1
items.risk: low: mechanical, and a stale lockfile fails the build instead of re-resolving
items.outcome: Merged 2026-11-22 as #19850. Pins the wasm lane only; measured with the real build tool and legacy-plan, 75 packages change and the only difference is the removal of unpinned:wasm. No key changes.

items.title: M0: pin `rust` (the lane the wasm closures are waiting on)
items.why: Found while measuring K-04: a package is `unpinned` if ANY language in its closure is, and 74 of 75 wasm crates depend on code/packages/rust/*. So wasm can never leave the class alone, and rust is about 29% of build time by the census's own figures. Its workspace Cargo.lock is already committed and already satisfies `cargo metadata --locked`.
items.scope: ~1471 cargo lines in code/packages/rust/*/BUILD and BUILD_windows; pinned.json
items.risk: medium: mechanical but wide; the whole rust lane becomes affected in one PR, so CI cost is the real cost
items.note: PR #19854: the code is correct (metadata contracts, Kiln sandbox, Ubuntu and Windows builds all green on 3e393962) but the macOS job exceeded GitHub's 6-hour job cap and was cancelled, so CI gate failed. Split into subset PRs of ~300-400 packages; see the lesson and K-15.

items.title: CHANGELOG.d/_meta.md does not state the shard filename rule
items.why: Found by losing a CI cycle on PR #19849: the name must be ^[0-9]{5}-[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*-[0-9a-f]{8}\.md$ (uppercase slug, lowercase hex digest, enforced by human-language-data/src/doc-shard.ts). _meta.md only says 'each numbered Markdown file is one entry'.
items.outcome: Merged 2026-11-24 as #19867 together with K-16. CHANGELOG.d/_meta.md now states the NNNNN-SLUG-HEX8 pattern and that zero is not a valid rank.

items.title: KILN01: the BUILD/rule language grammar and expansion spec
items.why: Referenced by KILN00 6, KILN02 (semantics version 1 is reserved for it) and KILN04, but the file does not exist. M4's rule files and the legacy-BUILD translator cannot be written without it, and 'specs first' means it lands before them.
items.risk: low mechanically, but it decides design; expect owner review
items.outcome: Merged 2026-11-23 as #19863. The first CI run failed on a lesson-heading test because the branch stacked on the lesson commit; the lesson commit was fixed and the branch rebased onto main with only the KILN01 commit.

items.title: Ledger snapshot rollback defence: refuse a snapshot older than the high-water mark (KILN00 18 Q9)
items.why: An attacker who can restore an older ledger snapshot resurrects revoked passes. The open question names the candidate fix and has never been decided.
items.scope: internal/ledger (store, merge), KILN00 10 and 18 Q9, tests
items.risk: low: the failure mode is refusing a merge, which is fail-closed
items.note: Implemented as ledger.MergeOptions.HighWater + ledger.NewestSequence; Merge keeps its signature. KILN00 18 Q9 is marked answered; only the mark storage location is left to the merge job wiring.

items.title: Stale claim in the Kiln README: '`Ledger` and `Tools` ... are not built yet'
items.why: The Ledger is built and documented 60 lines further down the same file. `Tools` provisioning (M5) is genuinely absent. The file is the implementation contract, so a contradiction in it is a real reading hazard.
items.scope: code/programs/go/kiln/README.md line 44 (fold into another Kiln PR, not its own)
items.outcome: Folded into the record-merge PR rather than sent alone.

items.title: KILN04 14, residual risk 1: record a dying call that reads as an observed read with an unknown result (D35 follow-up)
items.why: Named follow-up: threaded actions (Go worker threads in a filesystem loop) stay unrecorded because a thread killed inside openat/newfstatat leaves an unresumed-call refusal. Each one is recordable share lost toward the kill criterion.
items.risk: high: it widens what counts as an observation, so it is soundness-bearing and needs the owner's review

items.title: PR 7 (Phase B parser conversions) and PR 8 (delete the old scanner)
items.why: PR 8 removes the cross-check oracle; KILN04 4.9 gates it on Phase B plus a 14-day / 200-kiln-sandbox-run soak with zero mismatches.
items.risk: high: deleting the oracle is one-way

items.title: stage-4 PR 3b: the kiln-record.yml and kiln-record-merge CI jobs
items.why: `kiln record-merge` exists but nothing calls it, so the ledger still has no writer in CI. Needs the census workflow's setup (trusted default-branch dispatch, pinned toolchains, strace, the sandbox probe gate) and must NOT copy the census's job-start stamp (KILN04 4.8: it stamps first and fails if strace is missing).
items.scope: .github/workflows/kiln-record.yml; a --strict mode; the merge job's ledger upload
items.risk: high: cannot be validated on a branch at all, because prepare refuses an untrusted run. Requires a trusted dispatch after merge, so it should be landed by the owner or verified with a follow-up dispatch.

items.title: An end-to-end emit test for the merge job
items.why: The merge's void and refusal paths are tested; an EMIT test needs a real `prepare` shard (trusted linux/amd64). It belongs with PR 3b and is the last unproven link between 'shards record' and 'the ledger has manifests'.
items.scope: a Linux-only test beside TestSandboxRecordCollect, plus the same in CI's kiln-sandbox job
items.note: The void half is already covered by TestSandboxRecordCollect; this adds the positive half: a clean shard is emitted and both manifests and passes read back off disk. Named in ci/assert_sandbox_tests.py REQUIRED so the sandbox job fails if it stops running.
items.outcome: Merged 2026-11-24 as #19868. First CI run failed because the fixture results file lacked the schema key the strict decoder requires; fixed and green. The test is named in ci/assert_sandbox_tests.py REQUIRED so the sandbox job fails if it stops running.

items.title: Pin rust in subsets small enough for the 6h macOS job cap
items.why: Whole-lane pinning is one affected set of the entire rust lane, and the PR build is unsharded (only the scheduled full build shards), so the macOS job was cancelled at 6h01m. Split by package directory into ~300-400 packages per PR, watching the AFFECTED package count (dependents included), not the changed-file count. pinned.json gains rust only in the last subset.
items.risk: medium: each attempt can still exceed 6h if a subset is dominated by a heavily-depended-on crate
items.note: Chunk 0 of 5 merged as #19872 (326 packages, 329 affected). Four chunks remain; the generated vos-sched-* packages, the rust_library.star rule, and pinned.json are handled separately. CI cost is the bottleneck: each chunk is a full rust-lane build (~2-3h) and the Windows job has flaked twice on infrastructure (a vos-sched-rr 20-minute negative-control timeout, then a chocolatey 503 for qpdf). Both are pre-existing and unrelated to --locked.

items.title: lessons.d/_meta.md does not state the sub-heading level
items.why: Found by losing a CI cycle on PR #19862: the lesson title is '#' and a body sub-heading must be '###', because the renderer demotes every body heading by one level and a '##' sub-heading lands at '###' colliding with the title. That broke test_render_has_exactly_one_heading_per_lesson (2143 headings vs 2140 lessons). _meta.md said nothing about heading levels.
items.outcome: Merged with K-11 in one PR.

log.note: Loop opened. Baseline verified on main eb7b54787d9: go build, go vet and go test -short ./... all clean in code/programs/go/kiln (13 packages). Specs on main: KILN00, 02, 03, 04 (KILN01 missing). Implementation: 367 Go files, ~96.5k lines, commands version/verify-vectors/legacy-plan/explain/record{prepare,step,classify-action,collect,census}/sandbox-exec. No `kiln record-merge` and no kiln-record CI job, so nothing currently writes a ledger entry.

First implementation attempt used `${{ inputs.x || 'y' }}` for the schedule defaults. REJECTED in review: in an Actions expression the string "0" coerces to the number 0 and is falsy, so a dispatch with shard_indices=0 (the documented default) would silently have recorded shards 0,1,2. Replaced with an explicit `SCHEDULED == 'true'` guard and `${VAR:-default}` in the shell; verified all three paths locally (schedule -> 15/0,1,2/runner; dispatch -> 15/0/fresh unchanged; index>=count still refused).

Closed PR #19854. Verified green: Repo-wide metadata contracts, both Kiln sandbox images, build (ubuntu-latest), build (windows-2025). Only build (macos-latest) failed, by cancellation at the platform's 6h job cap. Two real bugs were found and fixed on the way: generated vos-sched BUILDs had to be pinned at their generator (build_gen.rs), and the barcode-layout-1d lane evidence had to be repinned. Both fixes stay in the split PRs.

#19862 (lesson) merged after a force-push that fixed the sub-heading level. #19863 (KILN01) was stacked on #19862 and went DIRTY when the base squash-merged; rebased onto main keeping only the KILN01 commit and it merged. Both docs PRs had failed CI on the same lesson heading test, which is why the lesson fix had to land first. K-11 and K-16 are now one PR documenting both rules beside the directories that enforce them.

#19850 (wasm pin), #19863 (KILN01), #19867 (K-11 + K-16) merged. Two lessons learned about the repo own conventions: lesson sub-headings are ### not ##, and a stacked PR goes DIRTY when its base squash-merges, so it must be rebased onto main with only its own commit. Both cost a CI cycle and both are now documented beside the directories.
#19868 merged after one CI cycle: the results fixture was missing the schema key. Also learned that the assert script requires every sandbox test to be named in REQUIRED.
Landed the high-water mark as a library gate with 8 tests. The mark is a parameter, not a stored file, because where it lives is the merge job decision; the ledger only enforces it.

Chunk 0 merged (#19872) after a merge conflict with main in code/packages/rust/sha1/BUILD (main added the warrant harness lines). Resolved by keeping main lines and adding --locked on top. The Windows build failed twice before passing: once a 1200s negative-control timeout in the generated vos-sched-rr package, once a chocolatey 503 that left qpdf missing (setup exit 127). Neither is caused by --locked.
